title: Tim Dooley Politics — Policy Domain Index
kind: derived navigation and provenance view; not a second politics owner
purpose: Project the dated political compendium into policy domains without duplicating or upgrading the underlying evidence. Entry references use zero-based indexes into canonical_owner.entries and remain typed by the canonical mode/confidence fields.
rules: This file does not turn a research lead into a finding, a prediction into a position, a programme into enacted policy, or a symbolic model into an empirical alliance.
Current-world comparators document independently existing institutions or policy directions; overlap does not establish influence, authorship, causation or endorsement.
Unresolved issues remain unresolved until a recoverable Tim source is promoted into the canonical compendium.

current_world_comparators.relevance: Independent current-world comparator for Tim's May 2026 European digital-sovereignty programme. The European Commission's 2026 technology-sovereignty package includes cloud/AI, semiconductors and open-source measures.
current_world_comparators.boundary: Comparator only. It does not establish that Tim influenced EU policy or that the two programmes are identical.

current_world_comparators.relevance: Grounds the politics reader's distinction between proposal, adoption, delegated/implementing acts and implementation.
Grounds the Denmark governance example: legislation, annual budget and parliamentary scrutiny are distinct tasks within a broader separation-of-powers system.
